definitions.explanation: To return to a place or situation, often implying an unexpected or unwelcome return. Carries a slightly dramatic or emphatic nuance compared to the plain 戻る.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}が{三日|みっか}ぶりに{舞|ま}い{戻|もど}ってきた。
examples.english: The cat came back after three days.

examples.japanese: {故郷|ふるさと}を{出|で}た{彼|かれ}は、{十年後|じゅうねんご}に{舞|ま}い{戻|もど}った。
examples.english: He left his hometown and came back ten years later.

examples.japanese: やっと{解決|かいけつ}したと{思|おも}ったら、{同|おな}じ{問題|もんだい}がまた{舞|ま}い{戻|もど}ってきた。
examples.english: Just when I thought it was finally resolved, the same problem came back again.

notes:
{舞|ま}い{戻|もど}る is an intransitive godan verb. It is a compound of {舞|ま}う (to dance, to flutter) and {戻|もど}る (to return).

ASPECT (ている):
{舞|ま}い{戻|もど}っている indicates the resulting state of having returned.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- [place]に{舞|ま}い{戻|もど}る (return to a place)
- [place]から{舞|ま}い{戻|もど}る (return from a place)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {故郷|ふるさと}に{舞|ま}い{戻|もど}る (return to one's hometown)
- {元|もと}の{場所|ばしょ}に{舞|ま}い{戻|もど}る (come back to the original place)

The {舞|ま}い prefix gives the return a sense of lightness or unexpectedness — as if the person or thing fluttered back. Often used when the return is surprising, unwelcome, or after a long absence. More expressive and literary than plain {戻|もど}る.
